newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor sees exciting prospects in nickel.
newsitem.headline: Gencor sees exciting prospects in nickel.

text.p: Gencor Ltd, flush from gaining control of Colombia's Cerro Matoso nickel mine, expects more growth in its nickel interests in future, chairman Brian Gilbertson said on Tuesday.
Gencor said last week it had upped its stake in Cerro Matoso to 98.9 percent and that it had started a feasibility study which could see the mine doubling its current production.
In addition to Colombia, there were promising developments at the Maggie Hays nickel deposit in Western Australia -- owned jointly with Forestania Gold NL, Gilbertson told Reuters.
"I think in future you are going to see nickel grow much stronger," Gilbertson said in an interview.
"Nickel is a much more volatile commodity, from the studies we have done, than the ones we are used to. So we are a little nervous about it.
"And Voisey's Bay is a monster elephant sitting out there with huge potential for the future," Gilbertson added.

Canadian nickel producer Inco Ltd last year won control of Voisey's Bay -- estimated to hold more than 150 million tonnes of high grade nickel, copper and cobalt ore which could be extracted at very low cost.
But Gilbertson said Gencor believed that Cerro Matoso could be among the lowest producers in the world.
"If we look at all of the projects that we know of in the world, with the possible exception of Voisey's Bay...we think Cerro Matoso as brownfields expansion is the cheapest in the world.
"If the nickel price disappears, it will be one of the last to go," he said, adding: "We are very, very pleased, it is a good deal".
Gencor subsidiary Billiton BVI Ltd paid $165.8 million for the stake in Cerro Matoso -- the world's fourth-largest nickel producer.
Cerro Matoso produced just over 50 million pounds of high quality nickel in 1996 for sale to the stainless steel industry.
Gencor says the mine can continue operating until at least 2027 and probably to 2041.
